compiled_prompt:
[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural image.
Keep the reference plate's exact composition: every edge, horizon line, and object position stays where it is.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   Peripheral urban specimens of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Canopy state for late September displays early autumn phenology: dense crowns transitioning from deep green to muted ochre and olive-yellow margins, with localized foliage thinning along upper outer branches.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (4500K Mid-morning raking sunlight):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is behind the camera and to the LEFT, out of frame (True Azimuth 106.0°, Elevation 10.5°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: all camera-facing facades are in full direct sunlight; left-facing walls are brightly lit and right-facing walls are in deep shadow.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: cast shadows project diagonally away from the camera toward the upper-RIGHT.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Every cast shadow is 5.4 times as long as the height of the object casting it. A 100 m tower casts a 542 m shadow. Apply this ratio to every object in the scene.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that cast shadows project diagonally away from the camera toward the upper-RIGHT. Every shadow must be angled toward the RIGHT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Edinburgh West End streetscape along Shandwick Place. Multi-storey Victorian Renaissance and Scots Baronial commercial tenement blocks constructed from droved and polished Craigleith buff sandstone ashlar and laminated Hailes grey sandstone. Detailed stone facades featuring strapwork gables, corbelled corner projections, moulded architraves, canted bay stacks, and Ballachulish blue-grey slate mansard roofs with pedimented dormers. Ground-floor street-level shopfronts with timber fascias, polished granite pilasters, and plate glass glazing. In the western axial view, the tall Italian Romanesque campanile of St George's West Church rises in tiered sandstone ashlar with arcaded belfry openings, machicolated cornice, and an octagonal pyramidal spire clad in verdigris-oxidized copper sheet. Continuous urban street wall displaying historical coal-smoke gypsum encrustations in carved recesses contrasted with rain-washed buff stone planes. Carriageway composed of smooth dense bitumen asphalt bisected by embedded grooved steel tramway rails flush with surface concrete track slabs, bounded by tooled grey Aberdeen granite kerbstones and broad Caithness flagstone footways. Solitary mature Acer pseudoplatanus street trees displaying late-September senescence with olive and ochre-flecked leaf canopies. Zero pedestrians, zero vehicles, pure static civic architectural fabric.
